An airbag inflator that ruptures can create a risk of injury or death. 

Corrective Actions: 
General Motors will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the driver-front airbag module.

2026250.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the instrument cluster not to display when the vehicle is started. As a result, you may not be able to see certain information about the vehicle, including the speedometer, gear selection indicators, warning lights and malfunction tell-tales. 

Safety Risk: 
Warnings, tell-tales and gauges that don't display could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Nissan will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the instrument cluster software.

2026251.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the weight sensor for the front passenger seat may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the passenger-front airbag and knee airbag could deploy in a crash that doesn't require them to. 
Note: This recall is an expansion of Transport Canada recall no. 2024-059. If the weight sensor fails, the SRS warning light would turn on in the instrument panel. 

Safety Risk: 
An airbag system that doesn't work properly could increase the risk of injury in a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
The company will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the passenger-front seat weight sensor.

2026257.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, there could be a problem with the driver and/or front passenger seatbelt pretensioner(s). As a result, the airbag warning light could turn on, and the seatbelt pretensioners could deploy without a crash. 
Note: This recall replaces Transport Canada recall nos. 2024-084 and 2025-164. Vehicles that were repaired under those recalls also require this inspection or repair.
 
Safety Risk: 
Seat belt pretensioners that don't work properly could create an increased risk of injury. Additionally, seat belt pretensioners that deploy without a crash could startle the driver and increase the risk of a crash.  
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the driver and front passenger seatbelt retractors.

2026258.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the engine may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the engine could fail and cause a loss of power to the wheels. 
Note: This recall only affects certain vehicles equipped with a 2.3 L engine.

Safety Risk: 
A sudden loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the engine.

2026259.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the front lower ball joint(s) may not have been installed correctly on the steering knuckle(s). As a result, the front lower ball joint(s) could separate and cause a loss of steering control.

Safety Risk: 
A loss of steering control could create a risk of a crash.  

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk Ford advises you not to drive your vehicle until the recall repairs are completed. Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to contact a dealer to arrange for an inspection. The dealer will repair the front steering knuckle(s), as necessary.

2026261.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the combination meter in the instrument cluster not to display when the vehicle is started. As a result, you may not be able to see certain information about the vehicle, including warning lights and malfunction tell-tales.
Note: This recall only affects vehicles equipped with a 12.3-inch display.  

Safety Risk: 
Warnings, tell-tales and gauges that don't display could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
The company will notify owners by mail and send a wireless over-the-air software update to eligible vehicles to update the combination meter software. Alternatively, you may schedule an appointment to have the update performed at a dealership.

2026266.summary:
Issue: 
On a small number of vehicles, the bolts that attach the rear passenger seat belt may not have been properly tightened. As a result, the seat belts could loosen or detach in a crash. 

Safety Risk: 
A seat belt that detaches in a crash could increase the risk of injury. 

Corrective Actions: 
Mercedes-Benz will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, tighten the rear seat belt attachment bolts.

2026271.summary:
Issue:
On certain vehicles, the connection for the electric hydraulic power steering pump (EHPSP) could become loose. If this happens, the EHPSP connection could overheat and melt.

Safety Risk: 
Wiring that overheats and melts can create a fire risk, even while the vehicle is parked and turned off.  

Corrective Actions:
To reduce the safety risk, FCA recommends that you should park your vehicle outside and away from other vehicles or buildings until the recall repairs are completed. FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the EHPSP and the wiring.

2026272.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the high-voltage battery could fail. If this happens, the high-voltage battery could overheat. 
Note: This recall only affects plug-in hybrid (PHEV) models. 

Safety Risk: 
A high-voltage battery that fails can create a fire risk, even while the vehicle is parked and turned off.  

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, FCA Canada advises that you should not charge your vehicle and to park the vehicle outdoors and away from other vehicles or structures until the recall repairs have been completed. FCA Canada will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the high-voltage battery. The dealer will also install an advanced diagnostic software that will monitor the high-voltage battery and warn you if it detects a problem.

2026274.summary:
Issue:
On certain vehicles, if the tire repair kit nozzle is not properly attached to the tire valve, pressure could build up in the sealant bottle. As a result, excessive pressure could cause the bottle cap to detach.

Safety Risk:
If the bottle cap detaches, it could increase the risk of injury.

Corrective Actions:
Honda will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the nozzle on the tire repair kit. If the sealant bottle has been previously used, it will be replaced.

2026275.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the suspension mounting points on the rear subframe could rust. As a result, rear suspension components could fail. This could lead to poor handling and a loss of vehicle control. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of control could create the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Honda will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and install a rear subframe reinforcement kit or replace the subframe, as necessary.

2026279.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the chrome plating on the center console could bubble and peel. If this happens, sharp edges can be created. 

Safety Risk: 
Exposed sharp edges can increase the risk of injury. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the center console.

2026280.summary:
Issue: 
On certain trucks, the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 17S35 (Transport Canada recall no. 2017-517) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a second repair is required.

Under certain conditions, the transmission gear selection indicator (PRNDL) may not work. Additionally, the transmission could shift into the reverse or neutral gear. This could cause sudden and unexpected vehicle movements.
Note: This recall only affects certain trucks equipped with a 3.3 L engine and a 6-speed transmission.
 
Safety Risk: 
A transmission gear selection indicator that doesn't work could create confusion. A vehicle that moves unexpectedly could increase the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your truck to a dealership to update the powertrain control module software.

2026281.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 18S07 (Transport Canada recall no. 2018-129) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a second repair is required.
Note: This recall only affects vehicles equipped with a 1.0 L or 1.6 L engine and a manual transmission.

On certain vehicles, repeated clutch slipping could cause the pressure plate to fracture. If this happens, transmission fluid could leak onto hot components in the engine compartment.  
 
Safety Risk: 
Oil that leaks onto hot components can create the risk of a fire. Additionally, an oil leak could create a hazard for others and increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the system software to detect and prevent prolonged clutch slip. For certain vehicles, the dealer will also inspect and, if necessary, replace the clutch assembly.

2026283.summary:
Issue:
On certain trucks, the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 24S37 (Transport Canada recall no. 2024-346) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain trucks, a problem with the output shaft speed sensor could cause the transmission to downshift suddenly to first gear. If this happens, there could be a loss of control. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of control could create the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your truck to a dealership to update the powertrain control module software.

2026286.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 17C01 (Transport Canada recall no. 2017-040) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the instrument panel cluster screen not to display when the vehicle is started. As a result, you may not be able to see certain information about the vehicle, including the gear selection, speedometer, warning lights and malfunction tell-tales. 

Safety Risk: 
Warnings, gauges, gear selection and tell-tales indicators that don't display could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the instrument panel cluster software.

2026287.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 19C03 (Transport Canada recall no. 2019-064) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the instrument panel cluster screen not to display when the vehicle is started. As a result, you may not be able to see certain information about the vehicle, including the gear selection, speedometer, warning lights and malfunction tell-tales. 

Safety Risk: 
Warnings, gauges, gear selection and tell-tales indicators that don't display could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the instrument panel cluster software.

2026288.summary:
Issue: 
On certain trucks, the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 20C03 (Transport Canada recall no. 2020-071) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain trucks, a software problem could cause the daytime running lamps (DRLs) to remain on when switching the master lighting switch from the ''Autolamp'' position to the ''headlamp on'' position. Canadian regulations require the DRLs to turn off when the headlamps are switched on.

Safety Risk: 
Daytime running lamps that stay on could cause glare for oncoming drivers and increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your truck to a dealership to update the body control module  software.

2026291.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 16C12 (Transport Canada recall no. 2016-410) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain vehicles, the window automatic reversal system may not react correctly after detecting an obstruction. As a result, the window could close with too much force before it stops and retracts.

Safety risk: 
A window that closes with excessive force could pinch a person and create a risk of injury. 

Corrective Actions:
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the power window automatic reversal system software.

2026292.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the connector for the driver-front airbag in the steering wheel could corrode. As a result, the driver-front airbag may not inflate in a crash. 
Note: This problem would cause the airbag warning light to turn on. 

Safety Risk: 
An airbag that doesn't work properly could increase the risk of injury in a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Land Rover will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to apply grease to the driver's airbag connector terminals.

2026302.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, when using the power folding function, the third-row seats may not automatically reverse if an obstruction is detected. As a result, occupants or objects could become trapped between the seat and the seatback.
 
 Safety Risk: 
A folding seatback that doesn't reverse could increase the risk of injury.  
 
Corrective actions: 
General Motors will notify owners by mail. As an interim repair, a dealer will disable the third-row power folding function. Once the final repair is available, General Motors will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to reprogram the third-row seat module.

2026304.summary:
Issue: 
On a small number of vehicles, a body panel behind the right tail light housing may not have been sealed properly. As a result, water could leak into the trunk and cause the park distance control and electronic power steering not to work. Additionally, over time, wiring in the trunk could become damaged and cause a short circuit or electrical arcing (sparks). 
Note: This problem would cause a warning to display in the instrument cluster. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of power steering assist can cause a sudden increase in steering effort, especially at low speeds, and increase the risk of a crash. A short circuit or electrical arcing can create the risk of a fire or injury. 

Corrective Actions: 
None of the affected vehicles have been delivered to customers. BMW will instruct dealers to inspect and, if necessary, apply seam sealer to the body panel before each vehicle is delivered.

2026308.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the instrument panel cluster to reboot while driving. As a result, you may not be able to see certain information about the vehicle, including the speedometer, fuel gauge, warning lights and malfunction tell-tales.
Note: This recall only affects hybrid (HEV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) models equipped with a heads-up display.

Safety Risk: 
Warnings, tell-tales and gauges that don't display could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Hyundai will notify owners in writing and send a wireless over-the-air software update to eligible vehicles to update the instrument panel cluster software. Alternatively, you may schedule an appointment to have the update performed at a Hyundai dealership.

2026310.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the fender flare(s) may not be properly attached. As a result, the fender flare(s) could loosen and separate from the vehicle.  
Note: This recall only affects Bronco Raptor models.
 
Safety Risk: 
A fender flare that detaches from the vehicle could create a road hazard for others and increase the risk of a crash.  
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and repair or replace the fender flares, as necessary.

2026311.summary:
Issue:
On certain vehicles, a problem in the transmission could cause the parking pawl to become damaged. As a result, when the transmission is shifted to Park, the vehicle could move if the parking brake is not applied. 

Safety Risk: 
A parked vehicle that rolls away could create the risk of an injury or a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, Ford recommends that you should always use the parking brake when you park until the recall repairs are completed. Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the powertrain control module (PCM) software. The dealer will also inspect and, if necessary, replace any damaged transmission components.

2026315.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by an FCA dealer during recall A9C (Transport Canada recall no. 2025-590) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the daytime running lights (DRLs) not to turn on. As a result, the vehicles may not meet certain requirements of Canadian regulations.   
Note: This recall replaces Transport Canada recall no. 2025-590.

Safety Risk: 
DRLs that don't turn on could reduce visibility and make the vehicle less visible to others. These issues could increase the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the vehicle software.

2026316.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the electronic stability control (ESC) system and power brake assist not to work.

Safety Risk: 
A loss of power brake assist could cause a sudden increase in brake pedal force and lead to an increase in stopping distance. This could increase the risk of a crash. Additionally, an electronic stability control system that doesn't work could increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the brake system control module software.

2026317.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the differential pinion shaft could break and cause a loss of power to the wheels. This could also cause the vehicle to move when the transmission is in Park, if the parking brake is not used.
Note: This recall only affects rear-wheel drive models.

Safety Risk: 
A loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. Additionally, a parked vehicle that moves suddenly could create the risk of an injury or a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to repair or replace the rear differential assembly, as necessary.

2026318.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the software update installed by a Ford dealer during recall 25SA2 (Transport Canada recall no. 2025-547) may not be effective. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the pedestrian alert system not to work properly. 
Note: This recall only affects hybrid electric vehicles. This recall replaces Transport Canada recall no. 2025-547. Vehicles that were repaired under that recall also require this repair.
 
Safety Risk: 
A pedestrian alert system that doesn't work properly could create confusion and increase the risk of injury for other road users. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and send a wireless over-the-air software update to eligible vehicles to update the accessory protocol image module (APIM) software. Alternatively, you may schedule an appointment to have the update performed at a Ford dealership. For certain Nautilus vehicles, owners will be advised to take their vehicle to a dealership to replace the digital signal processor (DSP) module.

2026319.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a problem with the windshield wiper motor could cause it not to work properly in cold temperatures. If this happens, the windshield wipers may only operate at their high-speed setting and the windshield washing system may not work.

Safety Risk:
Windshield wipers and a windshield washing system that don't work properly can reduce visibility and increase the risk of a crash.  

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the windshield wiper motor.

2026320.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the headlamp assemblies could cause the parking lamps and daytime running lights (DRLs) not to work, or to flicker. As a result, the vehicles may not meet certain requirements of Canadian regulations.   
Note: This recall only affects vehicles equipped with premium headlamp assemblies.

Safety Risk: 
Parking lamps and/or daytime running lights (DRLs) that don't work properly could make the vehicle less visible to other road users. This could increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions:
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect, and if necessary, replace the headlamp assemblies.

2026321.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by a BMW dealer during Transport Canada recall number 2024-456 may not have been done correctly. As a result, another repair is required.

On certain vehicles, a problem with the integrated brake system could cause reduced power brake assist. As a result, there may be reduced braking, and the antilock braking system (ABS) and dynamic stability control (DSC) may not work. 

Safety Risk: 
Reduced braking can cause extended stopping distances and could increase the risk of a crash. Additionally, antilock brakes and stability control systems that don't work could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
The company will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the integrated brake system.

2026324.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the rear outboard seat belts may contain defective automatic locking retractors (ALR). As a result, the seat belts may not properly lock to secure a child seat. 
Note: The vehicle's lower universal anchorage system (UAS) is not affected by this defect and may still be used to secure a child seat. 

Safety Risk: 
A seat belt that is used to secure a child restraint but is not properly locked could increase the risk of injury in a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, Nissan recommends using the vehicle's UAS system when securing a child seat.  Nissan will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the rear outboard seat belt(s).

2026325.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the rear subframe bolt(s) may not have been tightened properly. As a result, the bolt(s) could loosen and the rear subframe could detach. This could lead to poor handling and a loss of vehicle control. 

Safety Risk: 
Poor handling and a loss of control can create the risk of a crash. A rear subframe that detaches from the vehicle could create a road hazard for others and increase the risk of a crash.  

Corrective Actions: 
Honda will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace and/or tighten the rear subframe bolt(s).

2026326.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by a Honda dealer during recall O38 (Transport Canada recall no. 2020-345) may not be effective. As a result, certain vehicles require a second repair.

On certain vehicles, moisture could enter the rearview camera and cause it not to work properly. If this happens, the rearview image may be distorted or not display at all. Also, the camera image may not appear in certain bright light conditions.  
Note: This recall replaces recall O38 (Transport Canada recall no. 2020-345). Vehicles that were repaired under that recall also require this repair.

 Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display properly could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Honda will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealer to replace the rearview camera.

2026327.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by a Kia dealer during service campaign RC207 (Transport Canada recall number 2024-323) may not have been done correctly and/or may not be effective. As a result, another repair is required.

Under certain conditions, the switch for the driver- and/or passenger-front power seat motor(s) could become stuck and cause the seat motor(s) not to stop. If this happens, the motor(s) could overheat. 
Note: This recall replaces Transport Canada recall no. 2024-323. Vehicles that were repaired under that recall also require this repair. 

Safety Risk: 
A seat motor that overheats can create a fire risk, even while the vehicle is parked and turned off. 
 
Corrective actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, Kia advises that you should park your vehicle outdoors and away from other vehicles or structures until the recall repairs have been completed. Kia will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to install an electronic fuse for the power seats.

2026328.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the exterior B-pillar trims on the front and rear driver-side and passenger-side doors may not be properly attached. As a result, the trim(s) could loosen and separate from the vehicle. 
Note: This recall replaces Transport Canada recall no. 2025-588.
 
Safety Risk: 
Trim that detaches from the vehicle could create a hazard for others and increase the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to secure the exterior B-pillar trims.

2026329.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the compliance label lists an incorrect gross axle weight rating (GAWR). This could lead you to overload the vehicle, which could cause poor handling or a tire failure. 
Note: For the Forester model, this recall affects both gas and hybrid models. For the Crosstrek model, only the Crosstrek Hybrid model is affected. 

Safety Risk: 
Poor handling or a tire failure could cause a loss of control and increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Subaru will mail a new compliance label to each owner. If you'd like help to install the label, you can contact a Subaru dealer to have it installed free of charge.

2026330.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the rear axle carriers (knuckles) may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the rear knuckle(s) could break and separate at the toe control arm mounting point. If this happens, there could be a loss of vehicle stability. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of vehicle stability could cause a loss of control and increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
The company will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and replace the rear axle carrier sub-assemblies, as necessary.

2026331.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the engine starter may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the starter could overheat. 
Note: This recall is an expansion of Transport Canada recall no. 2026-040. 

Safety Risk: 
A starter that overheats can create the risk of a fire. 

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, BMW recommends not using the remote start function and not leaving the vehicle unattended with the engine running until the recall repairs have been completed. BMW will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the engine starter.

2026332.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, water could leak into the starter relay and cause it to corrode. If this happens, the relay could short circuit and the starter could overheat. 
Note: This recall only affects plug-in hybrid (PHEV) models. 

Safety Risk: 
A short circuit and/or a starter that overheats can create a fire risk, even while the vehicle is parked and turned off. 

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, BMW advises that you should park your vehicle outdoors and away from other vehicles or structures until the recall repairs have been completed. BMW will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the engine starter.

2026337.summary:
Issue: 
This recall is for certain rear center seat belt buckles that were installed during production or sold as a replacement part. 

On certain vehicles, the bracket that secures the rear center seat belt buckle may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the seat belt could detach in a crash. 

Safety Risk: 
A seat belt that detaches in a crash could increase the risk of injury. 

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, Hyundai advises that you shouldn't transport a passenger in the rear center seat until the recall repairs are completed. Hyundai will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the rear center seat belt buckle.

2026338.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 18S32 (Transport Canada recall no. 2018-577) may not have been done correctly. As a result, a another repair is required.

On certain vehicles, the canister purge valve (CPV) may stick open and cause the fuel tank to deform. If this happens, the fuel gauge could read incorrectly and there could be a loss of power to the wheels.
Note: This recall is an expansion of Transport Canada recall no. 2018-577. Vehicles repaired under that recall also require this repair. 

Safety Risk: 
A sudden loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the powertrain control module (PCM) software and, if necessary, replace the CPV. If the CPV is replaced, the dealer will inspect and replace the carbon canister, fuel tank and fuel delivery module, as necessary. In the interim, owners are advised to maintain at least 1/2 tank of fuel until the recall repair is performed.

2026339.summary:
Issue:
On certain vehicles the recall repairs completed by a Ford dealer during recall 25S67 (Transport Canada recall no. 2025-328) may not be effective. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain vehicles, the trim for the seat fold switch on the second-row outboard seats could become stuck. If this happens, the seat(s) could fold and/or move unexpectedly. 
Note: This recall replaces Transport Canada recall no. 2025-328. Vehicles that were repaired under that recall also require this repair. 
 
Safety Risk: 
A seat that folds and/or moves could increase the risk of injury in a crash.  
 
Corrective Action: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the seat fold switch trim and housing for one with an improved design.

2026340.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the driver's seat could recline on its own when using certain remote features including remote door unlocking, remote start and/or approaching the vehicle with the key fob. As a result, the second-row passenger could become trapped between the seat and the seatback.
Note: This recall only affects certain vehicles equipped with memory seats.
 
 Safety Risk: 
A seat that reclines on its own could increase the risk of injury and/or entrapment.
 
Corrective actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail. The corrective actions for this recall are under development.

2026341.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the repairs completed by a Ford dealer during customer satisfaction program 20N11 may not be effective. As a result, a second repair is required.

On certain vehicles, the roof rail covers could become loose and detach while driving.
Note: This recall is an expansion of Transport Canada recall no. 2021-267. Vehicles repaired under that recall don't require this repair.  

Safety Risk: 
A roof rail cover that detaches while driving could create a hazard for other road users and increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, secure the roof rail covers.

2026342.summary:
Issue: 
This recall is for certain integrated trailer modules that were installed before delivery or purchased from a dealer as an aftermarket accessory.

On certain vehicles, a software problem with the integrated trailer module (ITRM) may cause the trailer lights not to work when towing. This problem could also cause the trailer brakes not to work on certain vehicles.
Note: This problem would cause a "Trailer brake module fault" message to be displayed and turn signal telltale to flash rapidly.
 
Safety Risk: 
Trailer lights that don't work could make the vehicle less visible and cause following drivers not to recognize that the vehicle is braking or intends to turn or change lanes. These issues could increase the risk of a crash. Additionally, a loss of trailer brakes could increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the ITRM software.

2026344.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the compliance label may list the wrong gross axle weight rating (GAWR) information. This could lead you to overload the vehicle and cause poor handling or a tire failure. 
Note: This recall only affects models equipped with 22-inch wheels. 

Safety Risk: 
Poor handling or a tire failure could cause a loss of vehicle control and result in a crash. 

Corrective Action: 
The company will notify owners by mail and provide you with a new compliance label. If you'd like help to install it, you can contact a dealer to have it installed free of charge.

2026345.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, water could leak into the rearview camera and cause the rearview camera image not to display properly or at all. 

Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display properly could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Land Rover will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the rearview camera. The dealer will also add drainage holes to the tailgate trim.

2026346.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the steel wheel(s) may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the wheel(s) could crack and separate, causing a loss of control. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of control could create the risk of a crash. A wheel that separates could create a road hazard for others. 

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the steel wheel(s) and valve stem(s).

2026347.summary:
Issue: 
On certain trucks, the passenger-side mirror glass may not be attached properly. As a result, the mirror glass could fall off. 
Note: This recall only affects certain trucks equipped with a heated trailer tow mirror. 

Safety Risk: 
A missing mirror will reduce rear visibility and could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your truck to a dealership to replace the passenger side mirror glass.

2026356.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the engine wiring harness may not have enough protection and could become damaged by contact with surrounding components. As a result, the wiring harness could short circuit. 

Safety Risk: 
A short circuit can create the risk of a fire. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to install additional protection on the engine wiring harness. The dealer will also repair or replace the engine wiring harness, as necessary.

2026357.summary:
Issue: 
Under certain conditions, a software problem could cause the rearview camera image not to display when the transmission is shifted into reverse. 

Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Volkswagen will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the rearview camera software.

2026364.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, moisture could enter the driver-side door lock microswitch and cause it to corrode. As a result, the microswitch may fail to automatically engage the parking brake and/or the auto park feature when the door is opened. If this happens, the vehicle could roll away.
Note: This problem could also cause the radio and/or interior lights to remain on after exiting the vehicle.

Safety Risk: 
A parked vehicle that rolls away could create the risk of an injury or a crash.

Corrective Actions:
To reduce the safety risk, Mercedes-Benz recommends that you should always use the parking brake when you park. Mercedes-Benz will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the driver-side door lock.

2026368.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the left and right rear quarter window glass trims may not have been secured properly. As a result, the trim(s) could loosen and separate from the vehicle.  
 
Safety Risk: 
Trim that detaches from the vehicle could create a road hazard for others and increase the risk of a crash.  
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the rear quarter window glass trims.

2026369.summary:
Issue: 
Under certain conditions, a software problem could cause part of the rearview camera image to be blocked. Canadian regulations require the full rearview image to display while the transmission is in reverse gear.
Note: This recall only affects vehicles equipped with an 8-inch display and 360-degree cameras. 
 Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that is not fully displayed could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash.
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and send a wireless over-the-air software update to eligible vehicles to update the APIM software. Alternatively, you may schedule an appointment to have the update performed at a Ford dealership.

2026371.summary:
Issue: 
On certain trucks, the second-row seat belt anchors may not be properly attached. As a result, the seat belt(s) could detach in a crash. 

Safety Risk: 
A seat belt that detaches could increase the risk of injury in a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your truck to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, secure the second-row seat belt buckle(s) to the body.

2026373.summary:
Issue: 
On a small number of trucks, a component inside the high-voltage battery may not be properly secured. As a result, the component could move and damage the high-voltage battery. 

Safety Risk: 
A damaged high-voltage battery can create a fire risk. 

Corrective Actions: 
General Motors will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your truck to a dealership to replace the high-voltage battery.

2026374.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the steel wheel(s) may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the wheel(s) could crack and separate, causing a loss of control. 
Note: This recall affects vehicles equipped with steel wheels and/or a steel spare tire wheel. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of control could create the risk of a crash. A wheel that separates could create a road hazard for others. 

Corrective Actions: 
General Motors will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your truck to a dealership to inspect and replace the affected steel wheel(s), as necessary.

2026376.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the wrong airbag warning labels may have been installed on the driver and passenger sun visors. As a result, the vehicles don't meet the requirements of Canadian regulations.

Safety Risk: 
The airbag warning labels provide information about airbags and child restraint safety recommendations. Not following these recommendations could create an increased risk of injury. 

Corrective Actions: 
Mercedes-Benz will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the driver and passenger sun visors.

2026381.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the rear left and right outboard seat belts could become twisted and may not retract correctly. As a result, the seat belts may not work properly in a crash. 

Safety Risk: 
A seat belt that doesn't work properly could increase the risk of injury in a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the rear outboard seat belt retractors.

2026383.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the combination meter in the instrument cluster not to display when the vehicle is started. As a result, the turn signals and hazard lights may not work. Additionally, you may not be able to see certain information about the vehicle, including warning lights, malfunction tell-tales and seat belt reminders. 
Note: This recall only affects vehicles equipped with a 7-inch display. 

Safety Risk: 
Turn signals that don't work may cause a person not to recognize when the driver intends to turn or change lanes and could increase the risk of a crash. Warnings, tell-tales and gauges that don't display could also increase the risk of a crash.  A seat belt warning that doesn't work may not remind you to buckle your seat belt. Not wearing your seat belt can increase the risk of injury in a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Toyota will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the combination meter software.

2026384.summary:
Issue: 
On certain trucks, the oil reservoirs may not be properly welded to the shock absorbers. As a result, the welds could corrode and fail and cause the reservoir(s) to detach from the vehicle. 

Safety Risk: 
An oil reservoir that detaches from the vehicle could create a hazard for other road users and increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Toyota will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your truck to a dealership to inspect and replace the affected rear shock absorbers, as necessary.

2026391.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the connection between the driveshaft and rear differential could wear. If this happens, there could be a loss of power to the wheels, or the vehicle could move when it's parked and the parking brake isn't used. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. A parked vehicle that rolls away could also create the risk of an injury or a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, BMW recommends that you should always use the parking brake when you park. BMW will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect the connection between the driveshaft and rear differential.  The connection will be repaired or, if necessary, the driveshaft and rear differential will be replaced.

2026392.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by an FCA dealer during recalls Y73 and 20A (Transport Canada recall nos. 2021-663 and 2023-090) may not be effective. As a result, another repair is required.

On certain vehicles, the rear spoiler could hit the body when opening and closing the liftgate. This could damage the spoiler and cause it to detach from the vehicle.  

Safety Risk: 
A spoiler that detaches from the vehicle could create a road hazard for others.  

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to modify or, if necessary, replace the rear spoiler. The dealer will also inspect and adjust the liftgate, as necessary.

2026393.summary:
Issue: 
On one vehicle, a software problem could cause the windshield wipers not to work under certain conditions. 

Safety Risk: 
Windshield wipers that don't work could reduce visibility and increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify the owner in writing and advise them to take their vehicle to a dealership to update the body control module software.

2026396.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the rearview camera image not to display when the transmission is shifted into reverse. Canadian regulations require the rearview image to display when the vehicle is reversing. 
Note: This recall also affects Grand Cherokee L models and Grand Wagoneer L models.

Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash.  

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and send a wireless over-the-air software update to eligible vehicles to update the radio software. Alternatively, you may schedule an appointment to have the update performed at an FCA dealership.

2026401.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the low beam headlights may be too bright. Canadian regulations specify a maximum brightness for low beam headlights. 
 
Safety Risk: 
Low beam headlights that are too bright could cause reduced visibility for the driver and/or glare for oncoming drivers and increase the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Tesla will notify owners by email. The corrective actions for this recall are under development.

2026402.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, moisture could enter the rearview camera and could cause the rearview camera image not to display correctly or at all. 
Note: This recall only affects vehicles equipped with a standard rearview camera. 

Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display correctly could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
General Motors will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the rearview camera.

2026404.summary:
Issue:
On certain vehicles, the circuits for the exterior lighting may not have proper circuit protection. As a result, the wiring and components could overheat and melt, and the exterior lights may not work.

Safety Risk: 
Wiring and/or components that overheat and melt can create the risk of a fire. Exterior lights that don't work could increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, Lucid advises that you should park your vehicle outdoors and away from other vehicles or structures until the recall repairs have been completed. Lucid will notify owners by mail. Lucid has sent a wireless over-the-air software update to each vehicle. If you haven't yet accepted the software update, Lucid encourages you to do so. If you need assistance with this update, you should contact Lucid customer care or a Lucid service center. There is no further action needed if your vehicle has software version 2.10.0 or a later release.

2026407.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the rearview camera image to freeze or not to display. If this happens, the rearview image may not display when the transmission is shifted into reverse. Canadian regulations require the rearview image to display when the vehicle is reversing. 
 
Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display correctly could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Mitsubishi will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the infotainment system software.

2026408.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the engine wiring harness could become damaged. As a result, there could be a loss of power to the wheels, one or both headlamps could stop working, the windshield washer fluid pump may not work, and/or the engine cooling fan may not work.

Safety Risk: 
A sudden loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. A loss of headlamps and/or a windshield that is not properly cleared could reduce visibility and could also increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the engine compartment wiring harness ground terminals.

2026409.summary:
Issue: 
On a small number of trucks, the center high mount brake lamp may not have been properly attached. As a result, it could loosen and separate from the vehicle.  

Safety Risk: 
A center high mount brake lamp that detaches from the vehicle could create a road hazard for others and increase the risk of a crash.  
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and secure the center high mount brake lamp, as necessary.

2026410.summary:
Issue: 
On one vehicle, the battery tray bracket may not have been attached properly. As a result, it could move in a crash and reduce crash performance.

Safety Risk: 
Reduced crash performance could increase the risk of injury.

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify the owner by mail and advise them to take their vehicle to a dealership to inspect and secure the battery tray bracket, as necessary.

2026411.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the engine pistons may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the pistons may crack and cause the engine to fail. If this happens, there could be a sudden loss of power to the wheels.
Note: This recall only affects certain vehicles equipped with a 1.5 L or 2.3 L engine.

Safety Risk: 
A sudden loss of engine power could increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions:
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the engine.

2026416.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the rearview camera not to display when the transmission is shifted into reverse. Canadian regulations require the rearview image to display when the vehicle is reversing. 
 
Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the radio software.

2026417.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a problem with the brake pedal position sensor could cause the electronic stability control (ESC) system not to work. 
Note: This problem would cause the electronic stability control (ESC) warning light to turn on. 

Safety Risk: 
An electronic stability control system that doesn't work could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the brake pedal position sensor.

2026418.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the recall repairs completed by an FCA dealer during recalls 64A and 20D (Transport Canada recall nos. 2023-336 and 2026-037) may not have been done correctly or may not be effective. As a result, another repair is required. 

On certain vehicles, the rear coil springs may not have been installed correctly. As a result, the spring(s) could detach from the vehicle while driving. 
Note: This recall affects 2022-2023 Jeep Grand Cherokee and 2021-2023 Grand Cherokee L models. 

Safety Risk: 
A coil spring that detaches from the vehicle could create a road hazard for others and increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the rear coil spring lower isolators.

2026421.summary:
Issue:
On certain vehicles, under certain conditions, a software problem in the battery electric vehicle control unit (BEV ECU) could cause the electric drive system to shut down while driving. If this happens, there could be a sudden loss of power to the wheels.

Safety Risk: 
A sudden loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, Toyota advises that you should limit the vehicle's maximum state of charge to no more than 80% until the recall repairs have been completed. Toyota will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the BEV ECU software.

2026427.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the seatback recliners for the second-row seats may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the seatback(s) may not lock in position and could move in a crash. 
Note: This recall replaces Transport Canada recall No. 2026-101. 

Safety Risk: 
A seatback that moves could increase the risk of injury in a crash. 

Corrective Action: 
To reduce the safety risk, Toyota recommends not using the second-row seats to transport passengers until the recall repairs have been completed. Toyota will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the spring in the second-row seatback recliner assemblies.

2026429.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the passenger-side curtain airbag could become damaged when it inflates in a crash. 
 
Safety Risk: 
An airbag that doesn't work properly could increase the risk of injury in a crash. 
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to repair the bracket for the passenger-side curtain airbag.

2026431.summary:
Issue:
This recall is for certain vehicles that had a battery energy control module (BECM) replaced during service.
On certain vehicles, the replacement battery energy control module may not have been programmed correctly. As a result, the state of charge could display incorrectly, so a person may not recognize the low state of charge, which could cause a loss of power to the wheels. Additionally, this could lead to the high-voltage battery overheating after repeated fast charging.

Safety Risk: 
A loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. A battery that overheats can create a fire risk.
 
Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the battery energy control module software.

2026432.summary:
Issue: 
On certain trucks, the fuel tank strap(s) may not have been secured properly. As a result, the tank could fall and fuel could leak. If this happens, the engine could stall suddenly.

Safety Risk: 
A sudden loss of engine power could increase the risk of a crash. A fuel leak can create the risk of a fire. Additionally, a fuel tank that separates from the truck could create a hazard for other road users and increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions:
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the fuel tank strap(s).

2026433.summary:
Issue :
On certain vehicles, the pivot bolt(s) securing the roof crossbars may not have been tightened properly. As a result, the crossbar(s) could detach from the vehicle.
Note: This recall also affects certain 2023-2026 Wagoneer L models and Grand Wagoneer L models.

Safety Risk:
A crossbar that detaches from the vehicle could create a road hazard for others and increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective Actions:
FCA Canada will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and secure the roof crossbar(s), as necessary.

2026434.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, a software problem could cause the body control module (BCM) to reset while driving. As a result, the ignition could switch off and cause a loss of power to the wheels. It could also cause a loss of certain controls, warning lights, malfunction tell-tales and rearview camera system. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of power to the wheels, exterior lights that don't work, and/or controls, warnings and tell-tales that don't display could increase the risk of a crash. A rearview camera image that doesn't display could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up, which could also increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Volkswagen will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the BCM software.

2026439.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, one of the bolts that attaches the steering rack to the subframe could corrode and break. If this happens, the steering rack housing could break and cause a loss of steering control. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of steering control could create a risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
The company will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the right steering rack mounting bolt.

2026440.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the front steering knuckle(s) may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the knuckle(s) could break and cause a loss of steering control. 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of steering control could create the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Lexus will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the steering knuckle(s).

2026441.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the DC/DC converter could fail. As a result, the 12 V battery would not charge and a red "Stop Safely Electrical Fault Detected" warning message would be displayed. If this happens, and you continue to drive the vehicle, there could be a loss of power to the wheels and/or the vehicle's lights could turn off. 
Note: This recall is an expansion of Transport Canada recall no. 2026-195. Vehicles repaired under that recall don't require this repair. This recall only affects certain mild hybrid electric vehicles (MHEV). 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. Exterior lights that don't work may make the vehicle less visible to others and increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Jaguar will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the vehicle load balancing software.

2026442.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the DC/DC converter could fail. As a result, the 12 V battery would not charge and a red "Stop Safely Electrical Fault Detected" warning message would be displayed. If this happens, and you continue to drive the vehicle, there could be a loss of power to the wheels and/or the vehicle's lights could turn off. 
Note: This recall is an expansion of Transport Canada recall no. 2026-196. Vehicles repaired under that recall don't require this repair. This recall only affects certain mild hybrid electric vehicles (MHEV). 

Safety Risk: 
A loss of power to the wheels could increase the risk of a crash. Exterior lights that don't work may make the vehicle less visible to others and increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Land Rover will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to update the vehicle load balancing software.

2026443.summary:
Issue: 
Under certain conditions, a software problem could cause the rearview camera image to be blocked. Canadian regulations require the rearview image to display while the transmission is in reverse gear. 

Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Rivian will notify owners by email. Rivian has released an over-the-air software update to fix this problem. There is no further action required if your vehicle has software release 2026.23.0 or a later release.

2026445.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the second-row seats may not detect an obstruction when the power folding functions are used. If this happens, the seat(s) may continue moving even if there's an obstruction. 
Note: This recall only affects certain Ultimate Calligraphy models equipped with second-row captain chairs. 

Safety Risk: 
A seat that doesn't stop moving could increase the risk of injury. 

Corrective actions: 
To reduce the safety risk, Hyundai advises you to ensure the second-row seats are empty before using the power folding functions. Hyundai will notify owners in writing and send a wireless over-the-air software update to eligible vehicles to update the rear power seat software. Alternatively, you may schedule an appointment to have the update performed at a Hyundai dealership.

2026449.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the driver-front airbag inflator could rupture when the airbag deploys in a crash. If this happens, the airbag may not fully inflate and fragments could be propelled toward vehicle occupants. 

Safety Risk: 
An airbag inflator that ruptures can create a risk of injury or death. 

Corrective Actions: 
Hyundai will notify owners in writing and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to replace the driver-front airbag inflator.

2026450.summary:
Issue:
On certain vehicles, the rearview camera image may not display when the transmission is shifted into reverse gear. Canadian regulations require the rearview image to display when the vehicle is reversing.
Note: This recall only affects vehicles equipped with a 10.1-inch display screen 

Safety Risk: 
A rearview camera image that doesn't display could reduce a driver's ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash. 

Corrective Actions: 
Ford will notify owners by mail. The corrective actions for this recall are under development.

2026451.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the headlamp assemblies may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, on Super Duty models equipped with LED reflector headlamps, the daytime running lamps (DRLs), parking lamps, low beams, and/or high beams may be dim or may not work. On Super Duty models equipped with LED projector headlamps, the daytime running lamps (DRLs) and parking lamps may be dim or may not work. For Expedition models, the low beams and/or high beams may be dim or may not work.
Note: This recall only affects vehicles equipped with LED headlamps.
 
Safety Risk: 
Headlamps, parking lamps and/or daytime running lights (DRLs) that don't work properly could reduce visibility and make the vehicle less visible to other road users. This could increase the risk of a crash.
 
Corrective Actions:
Ford will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and replace the headlamp(s), as necessary.

2026453.summary:
Issue: 
On one vehicle, the powertrain control module (PCM) may not have been manufactured properly. As a result, the engine could stall while driving.

Safety Risk: 
A sudden loss of engine power could increase the risk of a crash.

Corrective actions: 
Land Rover will notify the owner by mail and advise them to take their vehicle to a dealership to replace the powertrain control module (PCM).

2026458.summary:
Issue: 
On certain vehicles, the second-row seat belt(s) may not have been stitched properly. As a result, the seat belt(s) may not hold a person in place during a crash. Additionally, the seat belt(s) may not properly secure a child seat.
Note: The vehicle's lower universal anchorage system (UAS) is not affected by this defect and may still be used to secure a child seat.

Safety Risk:
A seat belt that doesn't work properly could increase the risk of injury in a crash.

Corrective Actions: 
Land Rover will notify owners by mail and advise you to take your vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the second-row seat belt(s).
